headline: High: Prefect’s broad network egress can exfiltrate workflow metadata, while Pathway has no write/network surfaces to constrain the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway exposes no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, MCP, or browser surfaces, so there is no documented channel for Prefect to inject instructions into it. Prefect has broad network egress, but without a shared ingestion path the pairwise prompt-injection pathway is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later connects Prefect outputs into a Pathway parser or prompt field, injection risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except through typed, validated schemas.
Disable any future copy-paste bridge between Prefect logs and Pathway inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared message bus.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress, so it can transmit data off-host by default. Pathway has no filesystem read/write surfaces, so the main leakage path is one-way from Prefect rather than a shared workspace. The interaction is still meaningful because Prefect can externalize metadata without Pathway being able to constrain it.
conditions: IF Prefect is configured with sensitive workflow metadata, that metadata can leave the local environment over network egress.
mitigations: Redact workflow metadata before Prefect emits it.
Restrict Prefect egress to approved endpoints only.
Avoid placing secrets in workflow names, tags, or parameters.
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering on Prefect outbound requests.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, so it cannot contend with Prefect over shared mutable resources. Prefect’s profile does not show filesystem write or git mutation either, so there is no documented overlapping write surface to conflict over.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk should be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only with respect to shared repos.
Run them in separate working directories.
Lock any future shared mutable resource before writes.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutexes for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect is an orchestration tool that can act on workflow metadata, so if it consumes Pathway-produced outputs as authoritative inputs, errors can cascade into downstream automation. Pathway is document-processing oriented and has no built-in verification handoff to Prefect in the profile, so the pair lacks a documented guardrail against blind trust.
conditions: IF Prefect uses Pathway outputs as trigger data without validation, downstream actions may execute on incorrect information.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before Prefect-triggered actions.
Validate Pathway outputs against a schema before orchestration.
Mark Pathway outputs as untrusted in Prefect task metadata.
requires-engineering: add checksum or signature verification between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no stated residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Prefect handles workflow metadata, but Pathway lists no data classes touched, so there is no documented compliance breach pathway beyond ordinary deployment choices. The other agent is not cited for a specific mismatch because none is documented.
conditions: IF deployment policy requires a specific residency or retention regime, the operator must verify Prefect’s handling of workflow metadata against that policy.
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in workflow metadata.
Document the deployment region for any Prefect backend.
requires-engineering: add policy checks to the deployment pipeline.
